resources.string: Two permissions are needed: \"Nearby devices\" and \"Location\" (choose Precise). Android requires both to see the Bluetooth devices around you. No data leaves your phone.
Turn on Bluetooth to start searching.
If the button does nothing: open the app settings
Your phone\'s location is off: Android won\'t show Bluetooth devices until you turn it on.
Listening… Turn on or open the object you\'re looking for (earbuds often transmit only when out of their case).
Compass not available: the dots only show distance.
You are at the centre and the green area is in front of you. Turn slowly on the spot: hollow dots become solid once their direction is known.
Not detected yet: move closer or turn the object on
Turn slowly on the spot to find the direction (%1$d%%)
⚠️ It rings at full volume: don\'t do this while wearing the headphones.
Faster as you get closer. Volume: phone buttons.
Hold the phone flat in front of your chest and turn slowly on the spot (10–15 seconds): your body shields the signal from behind, so the cone can tell which side is stronger.
Then walk a few metres in the direction shown and turn again: the estimate improves with every turn.
The direction is an estimate: walls, furniture and reflections can shift it. Distance matters more than angle.
This is a paired device that isn\'t advertising: I\'m trying a direct connection to read its signal. It only works if the device is on and supports Bluetooth LE.
Connected headphones usually don\'t advertise over BLE: use \"Make it ring\" and search by ear.
Many earbuds transmit only when out of their case or with the case open. If the battery is flat there is no signal.
The PC must have Bluetooth on; on Windows open Settings › Bluetooth to make it visible.
